title: The Criminal Case Against Clavicular
dek: The looksmaxxing streamer is charged on Cape Cod with rape and drugging a 17-year-old. Here's the case, his denial, and the rap sheet that came before it.
body: Braden Peters, 20, better known online as Clavicular, built a following as the face of 'looksmaxxing': trying to max out your looks by any means, including, by his own account, steroids, crystal meth to kill appetite, and 'bonesmashing,' hitting your own face with a hammer in the belief that tiny fractures sharpen the jaw. Doctors call that a terrible idea. Prosecutors in Massachusetts now say he did something far worse.
Everything below is an allegation unless it says otherwise. Peters denies the Massachusetts charges and is presumed innocent.
## The Massachusetts case
On September 8, 2026, a criminal complaint was issued in Orleans District Court on Cape Cod charging Peters with three counts, after a judge found probable cause on September 4:
= Rape | Felony
= Drugging a person for sexual intercourse | Felony
= Procuring liquor for a person under 21 | Misdemeanor

The complaint stems from May 23, 2025, at his family's home in Chatham. According to the police report as described by the Boston Globe and CBS News, the complainant was 17 at the time. She went to Chatham police with a lawyer in June 2026. She alleges Peters gave her vodka during a livestream, told her to say she was 18 and to call the alcohol 'water' so his streaming accounts wouldn't get banned, and then had sex with her when she was too intoxicated to consent. Police wrote that they believed her level of intoxication left her unable to consent, and said Uber records confirmed his name and phone number. Police said they tried to reach Peters twice in late August without success.

Peters was summonsed, not arrested, and is not in custody. Reports of the maximum sentence vary: the rape count carries up to 20 years, while the drugging statute carries up to life with a 10-year minimum. A felony trial would require an indictment in Superior Court, and none has been reported.
## Where it stands

His October 14 arraignment was canceled. Reporting conflicts on when he's due back. NBC said the next hearing 'appears' to be October 22, Boston 25 reported that date is a hearing in a Florida civil case, and Boston's 7News said the arraignment would be the following week. He has not entered a plea.
> denies the claims and disputes the characterization of events (Peters' lawyer, via the Boston Globe)

His spokesperson, Mitchell Jackson, called the charges 'bogus' and argued they grew out of a civil lawsuit Peters refused to settle. On X, Peters posted that people come for successful young men's money.
## The civil suit

The same woman, now 18, is suing him in Miami-Dade County for more than $100,000. The suit alleges he injected her, while she was a minor and on a livestream, with Aqualyx, a fat-dissolving product not approved by the FDA, and that she was left with a perforated cheek. In October her lawyer dropped the sexual-assault claim from the civil case, saying that matter belongs in criminal court.
> this matter is more appropriate for the criminal justice system. (Drew Moss, the plaintiff's attorney)
## The rap sheet so far
= Arizona, Feb. 2026 · fake ID, pills without a prescription | Declined
Arrested in Old Town Scottsdale. The Maricopa County Attorney's Office turned it down, citing no reasonable likelihood of conviction.
= Florida, March 2026 · battery warrant, Osceola County | No charges

Arrested in Fort Lauderdale on a warrant. The sheriff's office said Peters instigated a fight between two women at a rental he'd booked and posted it to exploit them. Prosecutors later said they couldn't prove it beyond a reasonable doubt.
= Florida, May 2026 · firing a gun at an alligator in the Everglades | No contest
He pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public and got six months' probation, safety courses and 20 hours of community service that he isn't allowed to stream or monetize.
= Massachusetts, Sept. 2026 · rape, drugging, liquor to a minor | Pending
## The platforms

YouTube terminated his original channel in November 2025 and two replacement channels in April 2026. Kick removed him after a December 2025 livestream that appeared to show a person on the windshield of his moving Cybertruck; gaming outlet Dexerto later called that ban temporary. In April 2026 he was hospitalized after passing out on a livestream, and afterward said he was swearing off drugs.
## Why it matters

His fans are young. Doctors quoted by NPR and Fox News warn that looksmaxxing can cause serious physical and mental-health damage, and that teenage boys are especially vulnerable. The president of the American Society of Plastic Surgeons said even minimally invasive treatments carry real risks in untrained hands.

The Massachusetts case will be decided in a courtroom, not in a comment section. But the pattern of his public life is already on the record: arrests, a probation sentence, banned channels and a career built on telling kids to break their own faces.
